row.scim_plan: Acrobat for enterprise (Document Cloud for enterprise)
row.team_price_text: Acrobat Standard for teams: US$16.99/license/mo (annual, billed monthly)
row.evidence: Adobe's Microsoft Entra ID Sync (SCIM) guide requires 'Adobe products that belong to Creative Cloud for enterprise, Document Cloud for enterprise, or Experience Cloud', while the business pricing page lists only teams plans (Standard US$16.99, Pro US$23.99, Studio US$29.99 per license/mo) and sends larger organizations to Contact Sales.
row.notes: Still gated. Corrections to June: (1) June said the teams SKU supports SAML; Adobe's identity-types table marks Federated ID (SSO) and Enterprise ID as not supported for Document Cloud for teams, so SSO is also Enterprise-only. (2) The team plan is now the cheapest business tier, Acrobat Standard for teams at US$16.99/license/mo (annual, billed monthly); Acrobat Pro for teams is unchanged at US$23.99. (3) 'ETLA' has no first-party source on the pages loaded and was dropped from the plan name. SCIM is Adobe's Entra ID Sync and Google Sync only, on a federated directory; Okta's catalogue app is SAML only, so Okta and others need the User Sync Tool or User Management API (Enterprise). Prices shown are annual commitment billed monthly; prepaid prices were not captured.

scim.plan: Enterprise (Creative Cloud for enterprise / Document Cloud for enterprise)
scim.notes: SCIM is exposed only as Adobe's 'Sync' for Microsoft Entra ID and Google Workspace on a federated (SSO) directory; the Admin Console issues a Tenant URL and secret token for the Entra gallery app. The SCIM version and a generic endpoint for other clients are not documented. Federated ID (SSO) is not supported on Creative Cloud or Document Cloud for teams.

auth.token_source: Admin Console > Settings > Directory Details > Sync > Add Sync > Sync users from Microsoft Azure (Tenant URL and Secret token)

operations.notes: Deprovisioning only disables; permanent deletion requires an admin to enable editing of synced data (1-hour window) and delete in the Admin Console.

deprovision.data_retained: User is disabled (cannot sign in, shown as Disabled); the account and cloud-stored assets stay in the organization until an admin permanently deletes them.

custom.how: Adobe extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:Adobe:2.0:User with emailAliases, eduRole (Entra) and organizationalUnit (Google OU path, synced as user groups).

roles.notes: Synced groups can be assigned to product profiles in the Admin Console; role mapping over SCIM is not documented.

limitations.text: Only Microsoft Entra ID and Google Workspace sync are documented; other IdPs (Okta, JumpCloud) must use the User Sync Tool, the User Management API or CSV.
Requires at least one federated directory with verified domains; trustee consoles cannot use sync.
Nested Entra groups must be added to scope explicitly, and groups with HiddenMembership are not synced.
Synced users and groups are read-only in the Admin Console; editing can be enabled for 1 hour.

user_api.notes: Adobe's developer page addresses the User Management API to Enterprise customers; the reference is hosted on Adobe's adobe-apiplatform GitHub Pages site linked from developer.adobe.com/umapi.

auth.notes: OAuth Server-to-Server (client credentials) access token plus x-api-key header; JWT credentials are deprecated.

capabilities.notes: Licences and admin roles are group memberships (product profiles, admin groups) set through the action API.

endpoints.purpose: List users in a group or product profile
Action API: create, update, add/remove group and product profile membership, removeFromOrg (optionally deleteAccount)

rate_limits.text: Action API: 10 requests/minute per client, 100/minute per application; Get User: 25/minute per client, 100/minute per application.

google.notes: From Adobe's Google Sync guide (Adobe SAML app with Auto-provisioning in Google Admin Console); Google's own catalogue page was not found.

jumpcloud.notes: JumpCloud guide covers SAML SSO only.

okta.notes: Adobe Admin Console SSO (which covers Document Cloud) uses Okta's 'Adobe Creative Cloud' app, which marks SAML only (read from page markup). Okta's separate 'Adobe' (Acrobat online) app is SWA only.

fallbacks.other_sync: Adobe User Sync Tool (Active Directory / OpenLDAP); User Management API
fallbacks.notes: Automatic account creation on SSO sign-up is Enterprise-only, for federated directories.

conflicts.text: The Acrobat for business page lists 'Acrobat Express for teams' as the entry teams plan, while the plans and pricing page lists 'Acrobat Standard for teams' at US$16.99; the pricing page is used for the team plan.

open_questions: Adobe does not publish Enterprise (Creative Cloud / Document Cloud for enterprise) prices; seat minimums are not stated beyond the '11 or more licenses' guidance.
SCIM version, a generic SCIM endpoint for clients other than Entra and Google, token expiry, pagination and rate limits for Sync are not documented.
Whether disabling a synced user frees the product licence, and whether it ends active sessions, is not documented.
No OneLogin connector information was found on Adobe's help centre; OneLogin's own catalogue was not loaded.
No audit-log API or user-event webhooks for the Admin Console were found.
Google Workspace's own catalogue/help page for the Adobe provisioning app was not found (only Adobe's guide).
Acrobat 'Annual, prepaid' prices were not captured (the page defaults to annual billed monthly).
